cover_basis: Flooded, bunded paddy: surface runoff and splash erosion are near zero. A JICA Indonesia RUSLE report gives C = 0.010 for irrigated rice (seen in a search summary; original not read).
Upland rice on drained, usually sloping land: open soil between hills. Price and yield use paddy rice (item 27); national yield is mostly irrigated rice, so revenue is optimistic for upland rice.
Row crop with open soil early in the season. A JICA Indonesia RUSLE report gives C = 0.245 for maize (seen in a search summary; original not read).
Slow canopy closure; cassava is widely reported as an erosion-prone crop on slopes (FAO cassava erosion review, values not read). Assumed low protection.
Root crop planted on ridges; assumed low protection until the vines close the canopy.
Ridged root crop with a short cycle; assumed low protection.
Wetland taro in flooded plots; assumed high protection like paddy. FAOSTAT has no Vietnam price or yield for taro.
Annual row legume; assumed low protection.
Annual legume with a low canopy; assumed low protection. Price and yield are for groundnut in shell.
Annual legume. FAOSTAT has no Vietnam cowpea item: dry beans (item 176) are used as a proxy for price and yield.
Annual row crop with a sparse canopy; assumed low protection.
Shallow-rooted bulb crop on bare beds; assumed low protection.

Perennial with shade or understory. A Lampung (Indonesia) study measured C = 0.004-0.045 under cover versus 0.2 commonly used (search summary; original not read). Green coffee price and yield; robusta is the main species in Viet Nam.
Perennial tree plantation with leaf litter; no C value found for rubber. Assumed medium.
Perennial shrub hedgerows with dense cover; assumed medium.
Perennial tree. A FAO cassava erosion review is reported to give C = 0.1-0.3 for plantation and fruit trees such as cashew, coffee, oil palm and banana (search summary; original not read).

Perennial tree; see CSH for the C range of plantation crops. FAOSTAT item 249 has a Viet Nam USD price only for 2015 (LCU series ends 2018 with a 100x break in 2017), so there is no usable recent price; the yield exists but is not used alone.
Perennial tree; see CSH for the C range. FAOSTAT has no Vietnam price or yield for oil palm fruit.
Semi-perennial ratoon cane with a dense canopy once established; assumed medium.
Perennial; see CSH for the C range of plantation crops.
Perennial fruit tree; assumed medium. Oranges (item 490) are the proxy for all citrus.
Short-cycle vegetable on tilled beds; assumed low protection.
Short-cycle vegetable on tilled beds; assumed low protection. FAOSTAT has no Vietnam tomato price or yield.
Sprawling vine on bare beds, often with plastic mulch; assumed low protection.
